themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints spiked to 39 THIS WEEK—a 609% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 5.5 per week—signaling a rapid deterioration of road quality, potholes, or infrastructure failure affecting daily commutes and vehicle safety in Morrisania/Crotona.
evidence: 39 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (609% spike)
Z-score of 10.34 indicates extreme statistical significance
243 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (159 alterations) may indicate construction-related street damage
reporting_angles: Ground truth: drive or walk the district's major thoroughfares; photograph and measure potholes; interview residents about commute impact
Accountability: contact DOT on street repair queue times; cross-reference permit data with street complaints to identify construction zone overlap

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK—a 433% spike from the 0.8 weekly baseline—indicating a sharp increase in homeless encampments or informal settlements affecting public spaces and resident safety perception.
evidence: 4 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase)
Z-score of 3.92 indicates high statistical significance
Concurrent spike in illegal animal pet complaints (2300% up 2 weeks ago) may suggest unsanitary conditions in encampments
reporting_angles: On-the-ground visibility: map encampment locations from 311 data; conduct interviews with unhoused residents and nearby residents; document conditions
City response: request sanitation and social services deployment data; ask about outreach coordination between DHS and local nonprofits

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Sanitation Cascade
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped 248% LAST WEEK (10 vs. 2.9 weekly average) while residential disposal complaints surged 233% 2 WEEKS AGO (5 vs. 1.5 average), suggesting deteriorating waste management or pest control creating a compound infestation risk across the district.
evidence: 10 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (248% spike, z-score 5.62)
5 residential disposal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 baseline (233% spike, z-score 4.04)
Heat/hot water (3,984 complaints) and unsanitary conditions (930 complaints) are top baseline issues, creating compounding habitability stress
reporting_angles: Sanitation audit: interview DSNY about collection schedules and missed pickups in affected blocks; verify whether complaints cluster geographically
Health impact: contact NYC Health Department on vermin-related illness reports; interview residents about pest sightings in homes and restaurants

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction/plumbing complaints spiked 317% LAST WEEK (12 vs. 2.9 baseline) while water leak complaints remain elevated at 341 over 90 days, suggesting uncoordinated construction activity or aging building infrastructure failures affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 12 general construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (317% spike, z-score 5.17)
341 water leak complaints over 90 days (ongoing baseline issue)
243 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days with 159 alterations—may lack coordination with utility companies or building inspection oversight
reporting_angles: Permit oversight: cross-reference DOB alteration permits against 311 construction complaints to identify non-compliant jobs; contact DOB on enforcement
Infrastructure aging: request NYCHA/HPD data on building violations and repair backlogs; interview landlords about deferred maintenance costs

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal pet complaints surged 2,300% TWO WEEKS AGO (3 vs. 0.1 baseline)—the highest proportional spike in the dataset—indicating a sudden emergence of exotic animal ownership or animal welfare violations requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69—highest z-score in dataset)
No follow-up complaints reported since, suggesting either issue resolved or underreporting
May overlap with encampment surge if animals associated with unsheltered populations
reporting_angles: What was kept: FOIL request to 311 and NYPD for complaint details on animal type and location; contact animal control on enforcement outcomes
Neighborhood context: ask neighbors if spike was isolated incident or reflects broader exotic pet trend in the district
